newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Howard stresses Dalai Lama meeting religious.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Howard stresses Dalai Lama meeting religious.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Wednesday defended his willingness to meet exiled Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, saying it would be strange if he shunned such an important religious leader.
Howard hopes to meet the exiled 1989 Nobel Peace Prize winner, regarded by China as a crusader for Tibetan independence, in Sydney next week if their programmes allow.

"He is a significant religious leader and it's appropriate in those circumstances, as he's a guest in Australia, that I see him," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio in Indonesia, where he is on a state visit.
"It would be strange if I didn't, and I don't think the Australian people would expect me to spurn an invitation to meet him as a significant religious leader."
Howard's plans to meet the Dalai Lama prompted Beijing to warn on Tuesday of possible trade retaliation.
China regards the Tibetan leader as leading an international crusade to win independence for his vast but sparsely populated Himalayan region.
Howard would not comment on Beijing's threats.
"I don't want to over-react to it. I note what a spokesman for the foreign ministry has said and I'm not going to take it any further," he said.
"I've discussed the matter with the Chinese ambassador, he understands our position," Howard said.
"We value that relationship and we'll continue to work on it," he said.
The Dalai Lama, who fled Chinese-ruled Tibet in 1959, arrived in Australia on Saturday for a two-week visit.
He met Foreign Minister Alexander Downer on Saturday for unofficial talks and met several politicians in Canberra on Tuesday.
